name: Dom Pedro
description: Dom Pedro (Pedro) is a trick-taking card game derived from Pitch. 4-7 players (often partnerships). 52-card deck, 9 dealt. Bid for trump suit. Key scoring cards: Right Pedro (5 of trumps)=5pts, Left Pedro (same-color 5)=5pts, High(A)=1, Low(2)=1, Jack=1, Game(10)=1. Total 14pts per hand. Left Pedro counts as trump. Play to 100.

history.origins: Pedro was developed in the United States in the nineteenth century as a variation of Pitch (All Fours). The trump 5 (Pedro) is worth five points; in Double Pedro or Cinch the other 5 of the same colour is also a trump. The game was extremely widely played in the US at the end of the nineteenth century and declined in the twentieth; it remains popular in the southern USA, West Coast, Louisiana, Nicaragua, and in Finland as Pidro.
timeline: 19th century: Developed from Pitch/All Fours in the US.
Late 19th century: Extremely widely played in the US.
20th century: Declined with rise of bridge; remained popular in South, West Coast, Louisiana, Nicaragua, Finland (Pidro).
history.cultural: Popular in US and Canada; also played in Nicaragua and Finnish-speaking regions.
history.evolution: Many regional variants across the Americas and Europe (e.g. Pedro Sancho, King Pedro, 63, 83).

rules.objective: Be the first team or player to reach the agreed target (commonly 100 or 62 points) by winning tricks that contain scoring trumps and by making your bid; failing the bid sets you back.
